from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Strategy 1: The Principle of Extremity", [
            "Consider the extreme case first.",
            "Maximize or minimize the objective function.",
            "Boundary analysis collapses complex systems."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display 'Principle of Extremity' title: #00FFFF. Fades in.
        title_extremity = Text("Principle of Extremity", font_size=36, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(title_extremity, 'A3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(title_extremity))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate set of points: #FFCC00. Highlight max element.
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#FFCC00") for _ in range(20)])
        for p in points:
            p.move_to(self.grid['C3'] + np.array([np.random.uniform(-1, 1), np.random.uniform(-1, 1), 0]))
        
        # Find max (furthest right in this simple case)
        max_point = max(points, key=lambda p: p.get_x())
        max_point.set_color(RED)
        
        self.play(Create(points))
        self.play(Indicate(max_point))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFCC00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show shift/transform: #FFFFFF. Animate towards the extreme.
        self.play(points.animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Strategy 2: Combinatorial Invariants", 
                          ["Invariants remain unchanged by operations.", 
                           "Parity checks reveal impossible paths.", 
                           "Use color-coding to visualize states."])
        
        # Elements
        parity_title = Text("Parity", color="#CCFF00", font_size=32)
        grid_elements = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.6, fill_opacity=0.6) for _ in range(4)])
        invariant_text = Text("Invariant!", color="#FF0000", font_size=24)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(parity_title))
        self.place_at_grid(parity_title, 'A2')
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#CCFF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        for i, sq in enumerate(grid_elements):
            sq.set_fill(WHITE if i % 2 == 0 else GREY)
            self.place_at_grid(sq, f'C{i+1}')
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_elements))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(invariant_text, 'E3')
        self.play(Flash(invariant_text, color="#FF0000", line_length=0.2))
        self.play(FadeIn(invariant_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Strategy 3: Generating Functions and Recurrence", 
                          ["Translate recurrences into power series.", 
                           "Generating functions simplify term extraction.", 
                           "Algebraic manipulation solves recursive sequences."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        title_gen = Text("Generating Functions", color="#00FFCC")
        self.place_at_grid(title_gen, "A2", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(title_gen))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFCC"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        poly = MathTex("f(x) = \\sum_{n=0}^{\\infty} a_n x^n", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(poly, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(poly))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # Highlight coefficients
        a_n = poly[0][6:8]
        rect = SurroundingRectangle(a_n, color=YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(rect))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        new_term = MathTex("a_{n+1}", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(new_term, "E4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(a_n.copy(), new_term))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis & Summary", [
            "Identify the structure of the problem.",
            "Choose your strategy: invariant or extremity.",
            "Structured exploration always beats brute force."
        ])
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display 'Summary' title: #FFFFFF. Fades in.
        summary_text = Text("Summary", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(summary_text, "A3")
        self.play(FadeIn(summary_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF9900"))
        
        # List three strategy keywords: #FF9900. Reveal sequentially.
        kw1 = Text("Structure", font_size=28, color="#FF9900")
        self.place_at_grid(kw1, "C2")
        self.play(Write(kw1))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF9900"))
        kw2 = Text("Strategy: Invariant/Extremity", font_size=28, color="#FF9900")
        self.place_at_grid(kw2, "C4")
        self.play(Write(kw2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF9900"))
        kw3 = Text("Exploration > Brute Force", font_size=28, color="#FF9900")
        self.place_at_grid(kw3, "E3")
        self.play(Write(kw3))
        
        # Final checkmark animation: #00FF00. Appears to confirm completion.
        checkmark = Checkmark(color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(checkmark, "E5")
        self.play(Create(checkmark))
        self.wait(2)

class Checkmark(VMobject):
    def __init__(self, color=GREEN, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.set_points_smoothly([
            [-0.5, 0, 0],
            [-0.2, -0.5, 0],
            [0.5, 0.5, 0]
        ])
        self.set_stroke(color=color, width=8)

outline.target_audience: Advanced university students with a strong foundation in calculus and linear algebra.

sections.title: Introduction: The Putnam Mindset
sections.content: A brief overview of the Putnam competition: it's not about speed, but about elegant, creative proof construction. We introduce the core philosophy: reduction, symmetry, and parity.
sections.example: Visualize a 'Detective Cat' searching for a hidden pattern in a grid of numbers, turning a complex algebraic expression into a simple geometric symmetry.

sections.title: Strategy 1: The Principle of Extremity
sections.content: Prerequisite: Basic real analysis. We explain how to focus on the 'worst-case' scenario or the boundary of a set. By analyzing the maximum or minimum element, a complex system often collapses into a solvable proof.
sections.example: Imagine a flock of birds flying in a closed space; by looking at the 'outermost bird,' we prove that all birds must eventually be contained within a specific radius.

sections.title: Strategy 2: Combinatorial Invariants and Parity
sections.content: Using graphical visualizations (colored tiles or toggling light switches) to show how certain operations keep a property 'invariant.' This is critical for showing impossibility proofs.
sections.example: A robot navigating a 3D maze: show that the parity of its grid coordinates acts like a color-coded state, preventing it from reaching certain zones regardless of the path taken.

sections.title: Strategy 3: Generating Functions and Recurrence
sections.content: Prerequisite: Series and power functions. We translate a recursive sequence into a power series, allowing us to 'extract' the general term via algebraic manipulation.
sections.example: A 'Magic Fountain' machine where each new layer of water is determined by the two layers below it; representing this as a polynomial makes the water level at the 100th layer easy to calculate.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
sections.content: Connecting the dots: How to choose the right tool when facing an unseen problem. Emphasis on structured exploration over brute force.
sections.example: A toolbox metaphor: The student as a mechanic, identifying the 'Problem Engine' and selecting the 'Invariant Wrench' or 'Extremity Hammer' to solve the challenge.
